questions.prompt: What most distinguishes an end-to-end test?

options.text: It drives the whole running system like a real user, with nothing mocked

questions.explanation: E2E tests exercise the entire assembled system end to end, catching broken wiring that lower tests mock away.

questions.prompt: Why should end-to-end tests be kept few?

options.text: They're slow, brittle, and expensive to maintain

questions.explanation: E2E tests are slow and break on UI/timing/data changes, so you reserve them for a few critical journeys.

questions.prompt: Playwright reduces flakiness by ____-waiting for elements and retrying assertions, instead of using fixed sleeps.
questions.explanation: Auto-waiting waits for actionability and retries expect() until it holds or times out, replacing brittle sleeps.

questions.prompt: Which make E2E tests more resilient? Select all that apply.

options.text: Locating elements by role, label, or visible text
Using time.sleep to wait for content
Seeding test data instead of relying on pre-existing records

questions.explanation: Resilient locators, auto-waiting, and seeded data all reduce flakiness; fixed sleeps increase it.

questions.prompt: Order the steps a Playwright test typically performs.

items.text: Assert what the user sees (expect ... to_be_visible)

questions.explanation: Navigate, then interact via locators, then assert the visible outcome — with auto-waiting throughout.

questions.prompt: Match each Playwright locator to what it targets.

pairs.right: An element by accessible role and name
A form field by its label
An element by its visible text
A stable handle for elements with no natural one

questions.explanation: Role, label, and text locators mirror what users perceive; data-testid is a fallback stable hook.
